recent_notebooks.summary: Path dependence in value systems is structurally analogous to institutional liberalization and spatial boundary navigation. Divergence emerges when initial conditions constrain subsequent state-space exploration through path-dependent institutional or boundary feedback mechanisms.
recent_notebooks.title: Path-Dependent Value Divergence Mechanisms

recent_notebooks.summary: Continuous attractor dynamics, supported by entorhinal grid-cell representations, provide a robust mechanism for generating stable, path-dependent preference states from continuous inputs.
recent_notebooks.title: Interaction-Driven Attractor States as Stable Preferences

recent_notebooks.summary: Recursive feedback structures and stringent resolution criteria establish persistent relational states analogous to continuous attractor networks.
recent_notebooks.title: Relational Identity in Recursive Systems

recent_notebooks.summary: Accountability and consequence tracking in autonomous systems rely on structural boundary conditions and path-dependent feedback mechanisms that constrain state-space evolution.
recent_notebooks.title: Structural Mechanisms of Accountability and Path Dependence

review.alternative: Autonomous models may exhibit emergent behaviors that override initial structural constraints over time.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of convergence to identical outcomes across systems with widely divergent starting constraints.

claims.statement: Institutional design choices induce path dependence, where initial constraints shape long-term system evolution.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that initial choices (liberalization approach) constrain subsequent network evolution, suggesting a parallel for reasoning models starting with specific structural configurations.
support.passage: In this paper, we investigate the causes and consequences of institutional design choices in the liberalization of services trade and investment in preferential trade agreements (PTAs). We distinguish between a positive-list and a negative-list approach to services liberalization, and analyze PTAs signed by countries of the Asia-P

review.alternative: Conceptual mapping may rely on purely symbolic or connectionist statistical learning rather than spatial-like boundary representations.
review.would_change_mind: Proof that conceptual reasoning in LLMs operates without spatial-equivalent representational structures.

claims.statement: Geometric boundary representations in cognitive systems offer a structural analogy for how reasoning models might navigate conceptual constraints.

support.explanation: Entorhinal grid-cell representations illustrate how biological systems use boundary mechanisms for navigation, providing a potential structural foundation for mapping conceptual constraints in synthetic reasoning.
support.passage: Solstad T, Boccara CN, Kropff E, Moser MB, Moser EI (2008) Representation of geometric borders in the entorhinal cortex. Science  322: 1865–1868.
